payload.name: Preserve all explicitly enumerated facts about an object
payload.description: When a user message explicitly lists multiple purposes, functions, uses, or attributes of a single object or plan and a memory candidate is being extracted or updated from that message.
content: If one message explicitly enumerates several purposes, uses, or attributes of the same object or plan, include every enumerated item in the candidate; do not keep only one item or summarize away the rest.
Name the object exactly as the evidence names it; do not replace it with a different object inferred from context.
When updating an existing memory with an explicit list, preserve the full list from the new evidence while still removing facts the new evidence contradicts.

solves: Memory construction can fail when a candidate summary drops some of several explicitly enumerated facts about an object or plan, or when it substitutes a different object than the one named in the evidence. This Skill applies to future sessions where one message lists multiple purposes, uses, functions, or attributes of the same item and that message is the source for extraction or update. It does not apply when the message makes a single general claim, when the message concerns separate unrelated objects, or when an existing memory is merely reworded without introducing a new enumerated list.
